_provenance.house: hand-set prior, not a measurement: the curve Constituent Alignment used before v6.13 (expected break rate 3% in a safe aligned seat, 8% in a swing seat, 20% in a strongly opposed one; saturation 25 points), rewritten in the linear form a + b*alignment + b_opposed*min(alignment, 0) and applied to both parties. Since v6.16 the scale is in standard deviations per vote: the 25-point saturation divided by the binomial spread at the curve's swing-seat rate, 0.25 / sqrt(0.08 * 0.92) = 0.92151. Stamped with the current statistic so it stays usable before a chamber's first measured run

_source: Pre-first-run fallback only: the pipeline measures this per chamber every run (score_calculator.compute_constituent_reference — per-party fractional logit of break rate on seat alignment, kinked at a swing seat, scaled by the 90th-percentile residual in standard deviations per vote) and writes /data/constituent_reference.json, which takes precedence. These values are the hand-set curve Constituent Alignment used before v6.13 (expected break rate 3% in a safe aligned seat, 8% in a swing seat, 20% in a strongly opposed one; saturation 25 points, converted to standard deviations per vote at the swing-seat rate), rewritten in the linear form (a + b*alignment + b_opposed*min(alignment, 0)) and applied to both parties; no measurement of the live population exists yet to replace them. The first pipeline run does. Regenerate from a populated database with backend/scripts/calibrate_constituent_reference.py. The hand-set curve is not a measurement of any particular break-rate statistic, so it is stamped with the current one (config_definitions.CONSTITUENT_REFERENCE_STATISTIC; rerun this script or re-stamp by hand if that changes) and stays usable as a prior; measured references carry the stamp of what they were measured on.
